groups.defect: The Google Meet fallback in EventManager reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so it throws when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
groups.rationale: All five point at the same line in EventManager.ts and report the same missing optional chain. They all propose the same fix.

groups.defect: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar instead of the one matching the current credentialId, so secondary collective hosts write to the organizer's calendar. Lark and the base CalendarService have the same first-element selection problem.
groups.rationale: All six report the same first-element destination selection in Office365 createEvent at lines 73-76. s_d2d1c6a5 also says Lark and the base calendar service have the same problem, so the merged comment must carry that too.

groups.defect: In Google updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals the missing externalCalendarId, so it never finds a valid calendar. Updates lose their calendarId and deletes fall back to primary.
groups.rationale: Both report the same broken find() fallback at lines 254-256 and both point to the matching delete code at 315-317, so the merged comment needs edits in two places.
